cosy-lesson.title: What Would Happen If Everyone Refused to Work?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: General strike ≠ Work routine – a coordinated mass refusal to work across entire industries ≠ standard daily employment activity.

p.em: Example: A national general strike brings public transport and commerce to a halt, replacing normal work routine with civic protest.

cosy-blockquote.p: Unpaid care labor ≠ Monetized employment – household chores and caregiving performed without financial wages ≠ formal jobs paid with money.

p.em: Example: The 1975 strike highlighted how much society relies on unpaid care labor alongside monetized employment.

cosy-blockquote.p: Economic paralysis ≠ Business continuity – the complete shutdown of financial and commercial activities ≠ smooth ongoing operations of economic systems.

p.em: Example: A total work refusal by essential workers causes immediate economic paralysis, undermining business continuity.

cosy-blockquote.p: Structural dependency ≠ Self-sufficient isolation – reliance of a society on specific demographic groups or systems ≠ existing independently without outside help.

p.em: Example: Modern nations exhibit structural dependency on migrant labor, making self-sufficient isolation an impossible myth.

cosy-blockquote.p: Civic solidarity ≠ Individual indifference – mutual unity and support among citizens for a shared cause ≠ unconcerned detachment from social issues.

p.em: Example: The success of the strike depended on broad civic solidarity rather than individual indifference.

cosy-blockquote.p: Essential workforce ≠ Auxiliary labor – workers required to maintain vital public services and safety ≠ non-critical support staff.

p.em: Example: Sanitation and healthcare personnel form an essential workforce whose absence is felt instantly compared to auxiliary labor.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cross-border labor ≠ Domestic isolationism – employment involving foreign workers and international mobility ≠ restricting economic activity strictly within borders.

p.em: Example: Globalized cities rely on cross-border labor, proving that domestic isolationism leads to systemic collapse.

cosy-blockquote.p: Societal breakdown ≠ Systemic resilience – the failure of fundamental social institutions and services ≠ the ability of a system to withstand major shocks.

p.em: Example: A week-long total walkout risks societal breakdown if the state lacks systemic resilience to manage basic supply chains.

cosy-blockquote.p: Collective bargaining ≠ Individual negotiation – negotiating work conditions as an organized group ≠ making isolated personal agreements with employers.

p.em: Example: Mass strikes harness collective bargaining to achieve policy shifts that individual negotiation could never secure.

cosy-blockquote.p: Institutional vulnerability ≠ Operational stability – susceptibility of organizations to major disruptions ≠ consistent and smooth functioning of institutions.

p.em: Example: The strike exposed deep institutional vulnerability in childcare and schools, shaking operational stability nationwide.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
ACT I (Women): How did the 1975 Icelandic strike prove that unpaid care labor ≠ monetized employment is the invisible backbone of national economics? Seldom do governments calculate the value of unpaid care.
★ How would your family or household manage if no one performed domestic chores or childcare for three consecutive days?

ACT I (Women): What immediate institutional vulnerability ≠ operational stability would surface in healthcare and education if women walked out globally?
★ Have you ever noticed how many essential social roles in schools or nursing are staffed predominantly by women?

ACT I (Women): Why is a coordinated general strike ≠ work routine by women historically more effective at changing male perspectives than political debates?
★ Why do you think society often takes routine domestic labor for granted until it stops?

ACT II (Men): If all men refused to work, what form of economic paralysis ≠ business continuity would strike heavy industry, mining, and power grids?
★ Which physical infrastructure service in your city would collapse first if maintenance stopped?

ACT II (Men): How would a total walkout by male-dominated physical labor forces challenge our definition of an essential workforce ≠ auxiliary labor?
★ Do you think society values physical labor less than office work despite relying on it completely?

ACT II (Men): Could a refusal-to-work by men trigger a massive rebalancing of household responsibilities and civic solidarity ≠ individual indifference?
★ How balanced is the split of physical manual tasks versus administrative tasks in your own life?

ACT III (Foreigners): What severe structural dependency ≠ self-sufficient isolation do major global cities have on foreign-born workers?
★ If foreign workers in agriculture or delivery services stopped working, how long could your city maintain food supplies?

ACT III (Foreigners): How does a strike by cross-border labor ≠ domestic isolationism expose the hypocrisy of anti-immigration political discourse?
★ Have you ever lived or worked in a foreign country where you contributed to the local economy?

ACT III (Foreigners): Why do essential hospitality and sanitation services face near-instant societal breakdown ≠ systemic resilience when migrant labor halts?
★ How much do you notice the migrant workers who keep public transport and city streets functioning every morning?

SYNTHESIS: How does mass walkouts using collective bargaining ≠ individual negotiation redefine the balance of power between citizens and governments?
★ Do you believe strike action is the ultimate democratic right or an unfair disruption to ordinary people?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
Without recognizing unpaid care labor ≠ monetized employment, modern economic models will remain fundamentally flawed and unjust.
★ Should governments pay a standard baseline wage to stay-at-home parents and caregivers?

A 24-hour strike by women exposes institutional vulnerability ≠ operational stability far faster than any corporate union walkout in history.
★ Do you think a modern repetition of the 1975 Icelandic strike would have the same dramatic impact today?

Modern societies take their essential workforce ≠ auxiliary labor for granted until a general strike forces a breakdown of daily routines.
★ Which essential profession in your opinion deserves a significant salary increase?

If male-dominated heavy physical industries staged a total work refusal, economic paralysis ≠ business continuity would occur within 48 hours.
★ Could you survive comfortably if electricity and water services were cut off for two days?

Societies that promote political isolationism ignore their deep structural dependency ≠ self-sufficient isolation on international migrant labor.
★ Do you think countries should make it easier for foreign workers to obtain legal work visas?

A day without cross-border labor ≠ domestic isolationism would prove that globalized cities cannot function on native workforce alone.
★ Have you ever relied on services provided mainly by foreign workers in your daily life?

Mass public walkouts build genuine civic solidarity ≠ individual indifference that lasts far beyond the single day of protest.
★ Does participating in a public rally or strike make you feel more connected to your community?

Governments fear general strike ≠ work routine movements because they prove that power ultimately belongs to the laboring public.
★ Do you think citizens have lost some of their willingness to protest compared to previous generations?

Threats of societal breakdown ≠ systemic resilience during strikes are often exaggerated by politicians to discourage organized labor.
★ Have media reports ever made a strike seem more dangerous or inconvenient than it actually was?

True social progress requires collective bargaining ≠ individual negotiation to protect vulnerable workers from exploitation.
★ Would you join a labor union if one were active in your industry or workplace?

ul.li: Incorrect: If women would strike → Correct: If women were to strike ((Grammar conditional: Avoid 'would' in conditional if-clauses; use subjunctive 'were to strike' or past simple))
Incorrect: The strike → Correct: The strike ((Word order: Transitive verb + direct object + temporal modifier))
Incorrect: We discussed about → Correct: We discussed X ((Deletion / extra word: 'discuss' is a transitive verb taking a direct object without preposition 'about'))

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Reflection & Feedback: Review language highlights and key corrections with your teacher.
